text:
Jordan (support): Heads up — Greenline reported intermittent p99 spikes on embeddings endpoint starting ~2026-02-04 22:10 UTC. They see normal p95 ~120ms but p99 jumps to 1.2s for bursts >300 rps.

Maria C (runtime): Thanks — any customer logs or request IDs? did this start after a deploy? :thinking:

Jordan (support): Sent trace examples in the ticket, attached a cropped server log: 
```
2026-02-04T22:11:03Z INFO req_id=0xabc123 model=embed-large latency_ms=121
2026-02-04T22:11:04Z INFO req_id=0xdef456 model=embed-large latency_ms=124
2026-02-04T22:11:05Z INFO req_id=0xaaa999 model=embed-large latency_ms=1200
```
No config changes from customer side. Support checked they used same model version.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4873 (severity=3) — linked to ticket #PLAT-912.

Akshay P: I rolled a small canary on 2026-02-04T21:50 for a KV-cache change (cache eviction heuristics). Canary looked fine but not at 300+rps sustained. Might be related. :eyes:

Maria C (runtime): Good lead. Can someone run the internal loadbench against embed-large with the same concurrency pattern? Need p50/p95/p99 and kernel/queue metrics. Olivia?

Olivia K (bench): I can run a reproducer. Quick question — do we have the exact client payload sizes? Greenline said avg tokens ~32, but embeddings use 1k-dim vectors. I'll run 30s ramps to 400rps and then a 2m sustained at 350rps. Command I'll use: 
```
./bench_runner --model embed-large --concurrency 350 --ramp 30 --duration 120 --trace-kv --out=run_174912
```
Any additional flags?

Akshay P: Add --disable-auto-batch to see single-request path and --enable-kv-cache to toggle. Run two runs: one with kv-cache on, one off. Also capture /metrics endpoint every 5s.

Olivia K (bench): Got it. Will run both and upload results to the thread.

Liz S (sre): Adding system-side checks: I'll capture iostat, nvtop, and per-process sched stats. Also want to see kernel preempt_count spikes. If it's GC/alloc churn on the runtime side, flamegraph helps.

eng-runtime-bot: Perf job queued: runtime/bench/1749123456 — will post artifacts when complete.

Maria C (runtime): If kv-cache eviction changed recently, we should look for serialization pauses when cache misses cascade (KV population causing synchronous I/O or lock contention). Also double-check the batching queue length histogram — a sudden spike there would explain p99 tails.

Olivia K (bench): First run (kv-cache enabled) finished. Key numbers: p50=118ms p95=190ms p99=1.18s. Attached small artifact: perf-summary.txt (uploaded).

Olivia K (bench): Second run (kv-cache disabled): p50=120ms p95=180ms p99=125ms. That's a huge delta.

Akshay P: Whoa — disabling kv-cache drastically reduced p99. That points to cache population / locking problem. Thanks Olivia.

Liz S (sre): I grabbed perf maps and a short async-profiler snapshot during the spike. Top hotspots: runtime::kv::populate_sync and runtime::cache::lock_wait. Flamegraph link: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/flame/174912_populate.svg

Maria C (runtime): Looks like populate_sync is blocking the request path. We intended population to be async. Was there a fallback introduced in the canary that does synchronous fetch on miss?

Akshay P: Yes — the canary added a fallback that does a sync write for correctness when a memstore TTL is missing. The thought was correctness-first. I can revert that quick patch.

Maria C (runtime): Can you open a small PR with revert + unit test? Tag it with INC-2026-4873. Also add a config flag to force async populate mode for now.

Akshay P: Will do. Pinged @Olivia to re-run bench after deploy. PR in progress: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/1227

Jordan (support): I replied to Greenline that we're investigating and will update within 60m.

Olivia K (bench): Re-run queued post-deploy. Command: same as before, will attach updated p99.

eng-runtime-bot: deploy job started: canary/runtime-kv-revert -> 3 nodes.

Liz S (sre): Monitoring heap/locks during deploy. If p99 improves on canary, we can promote.

Olivia K (bench): Post-deploy numbers (canary): p50=119ms p95=185ms p99=140ms. Much better.

Maria C (runtime): Great — looks like the sync-populate was the culprit. @Akshay please merge revert + config. We'll schedule a follow-up to design a non-blocking correctness path (async write w/ ack).

Akshay P: Merged PR, rolling to prod in 20m. Will also add a gated feature flag for next iteration.

Jordan (support): Told Greenline fix is rolling, asked them to verify after 30m.

Liz S (sre): Closing incident draft, will keep watch for 2 hours. Add postmortem if customer saw > 1min outage or impact.

Maria C (runtime): Postmortem owners: Akshay + Liz. Please capture timeline, root cause (sync-populate), why unit tests missed it, and next steps (flag, async design, perf tests in CI).

Akshay P: Will draft. Thanks everyone for quick turn. :thumbsup:

Jordan (support): Greenline confirmed latency back to normal after 45m. Marking resolved on ticket side.

eng-runtime-bot: incident INC-2026-4873 updated to resolved.
